subject: Could inspect() not ignore parameter constraints?

messages.author: 8c2d79813f5db571
messages.subject: Could inspect() not ignore parameter constraints?
parts:
hi,

after reading the lavaan tutorial and testing the examples (and extensively so those on multiple groups and measurement invariance, pp.17-26) it appears to me that lavaan's
inspect()
function is not fully equivalent to Mplus'
TECH1
function or to the
Parameter Specifications
portion of a LiSRel output (if anybody is still familiar with that...).

It appears that inspect() disregards equality constraints (as implied on p. 37 of the tutorial and on p. 38 of the reference manual, under the "partable" value for the what argument of the lavInspect(lavobject, what="free") function) : "The non-zero integers represent both the ﬁxed parameters (for example, factor loadings ﬁxed at 1.0), and the free parameters if we ignore any equality constraints. They correspond with all entries (ﬁxed or free) in the parameter table."

Is it possible to obtain that parameter constraints are considered, so that the non-zero integers are repeated for parameters with equality constraints?

Actually, if I may, this option would be extremely useful and precious for checking that one has correctly specified the tested model - as such it may even appear by default on the output.

Thanks and best regards,
paolo

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Could inspect() not ignore parameter constraints?
parts:
On 09/16/2015 03:47 PM, Paolo Ghisletta wrote:
> It appears that inspect() disregards equality constraints (as implied on
> p. 37 of the tutorial and on p. 38 of the reference manual, under the
> "partable" value for the what argument of the lavInspect(lavobject,
> what="free") function) : "/The non-zero integers represent both the ﬁxed

> parameters (for example, factor loadings ﬁxed at 1.0), and the free
> parameters if we ignore any equality constraints. They correspond with

> all entries (ﬁxed or free) in the parameter table./"

That is correct, as of lavaan 0.5-18. It is a 'side-effect' of the 'big
change' (when it comes to handling equality constraints) that was
introduced in 0.5-18. The rationale behind this change is explained in
this document:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/notes/lavaan_eq_constraints.pdf

> Is it possible to obtain that parameter constraints are considered, so
> that the non-zero integers are repeated for parameters with equality
> constraints?

That was the case in 0.5-17. I liked that very much too. And this system
of 'repeating the parameter number' for those parameters that are
constrained to be equal works really well for simple equality constraint
(eg a == b), but it does not extend to more general constraints (eg a ==
2*b).

> Actually, if I may, this option would be extremely useful and precious
> for checking that one has correctly specified the tested model - as such
> it may even appear by default on the output.

I take it you are only talking about the output of inspect/lavInspect here?

I have considered the idea of showing the constraints (if any) somehow
in the output of inspect(). I will try something and get back.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Could inspect() not ignore parameter constraints?
parts:
In lavaan dev 0.5-21, we now add a 'constraints' element at the top of
the model matrices list. It shows a table of parameter numbers that are
constrained to be equal.

For example:

library(lavaan)
example(cfa)
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group = "school",
group.equal = "loadings")
inspect(fit)

gives the output below.

Yves.
